parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is the governing state's national framework, applied here with no documented local derogation. Visitor-facing exposures are limited: the documented tier-1-adjacent harm is birth-marker-adjacent prison placement of trans women in all-male facilities with assault threats, corroborated by the 2021 detention-watchdog finding of persistent serious violations across all state places of detention — an unremedied state-institutional exposure, but one that triggers only upon custody. No documented border, document, facility, care or police friction for trans visitors; protections (penal-code discrimination ground, aggravating factor, conversion-therapy ban) are operative national law. Marriage equality is a climate signal only. Layered protections with one conditional custodial exposure place this in the upper Reduced Risk band, below 0.85 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or document friction for trans visitors in the dossier.
entry_documents.protection: National framework applies unchanged; no local narrowing ordinance documented.
entry_documents.interaction: None documented between entry screening and custodial or care systems.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women placed by legal gender marker, in practice all-male facilities facing assault threats (2018 feature); 2021 watchdog finding of persistent serious violations of trans detainees' rights across all state detention places, by terms covering establishments here.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Placement follows legal marker, not anatomy; recourse machinery (watchdog) exists but findings unremedied since 2010.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visitor arrest or immigration detention routes into this state custodial system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Watchdog finding covers all state places of deprivation of liberty; hospital-ward placement not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None specific documented beyond national framework.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State penal/civil-status authority governs local establishments.

care_services.exposure: For residents: waiting times, inequitable access (2022 report); not shown to reach visitors. Pediatric-care politics ongoing but bill stalled and government-opposed.
care_services.protection: Affirming surgery legal since 1979; care within national health system.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Around 1,870 homophobic/transphobic attack victims recorded 2019 nationwide, combined figure, no trans-only or local breakdown — background-level signal only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 'Gender identity' discrimination ground in penal code since 2016; transphobic motive aggravating since 2017; conversion therapy banned 2022.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State law enforced locally; head of state publicly denounced anti-LGBT violence (2018).

minors_guardians.exposure: Senate bill to ban under-18 transition (May 2024) stalled, government-opposed; not law, not visitor-specific.
minors_guardians.protection: Late-2024 pediatric guidelines permit blockers from Tanner stage 2.
minors_guardians.interaction: Uncertainty about bill's future; no documented visitor-facing minor restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No collectivity-specific incident documented; nationwide combined attack figures lack trans-specific denominators.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime aggravation, penal-code ground, equality agency, prosecution possible under national law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: National police and courts operate here.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved whether watchdog findings acted on locally; no local inspection documented; local-variation unknowable from record.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented national protections in force; judicial recourse functioning in the state.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns are open questions (light weight), not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far safer: no visitor register, no entry exclusion, no universal-exposure measure documented; worst feature is conditional custodial placement, not routine border denial.

Safer than the 0.55 anchor: no documented secondary-screening or entry-refusal pattern at all; layered penal-code protections and hate-crime aggravation operate, whereas the anchor documents recurring humiliating screening.

Comparable-plus: entry is smoother than the anchor's discretion-heavy border practice; but the documented unremedied custodial exposure (men's-facility placement, watchdog persistence findings) is more concrete than the anchor's, pulling toward rather than above the 0.75 band.
Slightly below: the anchor documents care remedies operating; here the documented institutional failure is in detention, unremedied for over a decade, which the anchor lacks.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters the governing state's national regime unchanged: no documented local narrowing, no visitor-specific restriction, and operative national protections (penal-code gender-identity ground, aggravating factor, conversion-therapy ban). The single documented traveller-relevant exposure is state custody: trans women placed by legal marker into all-male facilities facing assault, corroborated by recurring watchdog findings since 2010 — a tier-1-adjacent harm under rule 21, but conditional on detention rather than universal like facility bans or border screening. Open questions (local inspection absence, stalled minor-care bill) are light. Result: comfortably in Reduced Risk, near the 0.75–0.80 boundary.
